fire: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: production 2D game animation sprite atlas for a hand-inked wilderness survival game. Create ONE transparent PNG atlas, EXACTLY THREE equal columns and FOUR equal rows (12 isolated equal square cells), ideally 1536x2048. Every cell has generous transparent gutters. No text, labels, borders, ground, shadow, scenery, frames or checkerboard. Crisp hand-painted shapes, tapered irregular ink accents, restrained texture, readable after downsampling to 64 pixels; no soft rectangular glow. Every cell uses exactly the same center pivot and scale. All projectiles point horizontally RIGHT (+X). Reading order: TOP TWO ROWS are six consecutive frames of ONE looping projectile head, THIRD ROW is three lifetime stages of ONE SMALL DETACHED trail particle, FOURTH ROW is three stages of ONE contact burst (small flash, expanded fragments, sparse fading fragments). Head art contains only the head and close wisps, never an attached long tail or loose distant particles. Head frames must maintain location and volume; only the material flickers/deforms. Transparent alpha everywhere outside painted shapes. ELEMENT FIRE. Head: compact asymmetrical living flame bolt, pale yellow-white hot tip/core slightly right of center, golden mid flame, burnt orange/red pointed short tongues curling to the left; dark reddish ink only along selected outer edges, not a black ring. Six frames have clearly different short flame tongues growing, splitting, curling, contracting into a seamless loop; not six identical cutouts rotated. Total head occupies roughly 55% cell width and 40% height; no face, no round gemstone, no fireball with long streaming tail. Trail row: a single tiny angular orange ember brush dash, then thinner red ember, then small dim rust fleck; all at the same center, about 18% cell width and 8% height. Impact row: short pale-hot star flash, irregular orange flame chip burst centered at same pivot, then sparse rust-orange sparks; directional impact mostly spreads forward right and a little above/below, maximum 60% cell width. The design should remain visually distinct from a purple four-point magical spark.
